_meta.indication: Treatment of complicated intra-abdominal infections and complicated urinary tract infections, including pyelonephritis, caused by susceptible designated microorganisms

pivotal_trials.trial_name: DORI-07 and DORI-08 (two Phase 3 cIAI studies)
pivotal_trials.design: Identical, phase 3, prospective, randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, multicenter trials comparing doripenem to meropenem
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with complicated intra-abdominal infections (946 randomized across the two studies)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Non-inferiority of doripenem to meropenem in clinical cure rate at test-of-cure (TOC)
pivotal_trials.n: 946 adults randomized across DORI-07 and DORI-08
pivotal_trials.result: DORI-07 ME clinical cure: doripenem 140/165 (85.9%) vs meropenem 133/156 (85.3%), difference 0.6 (95% CI -7.7, 9.0); DORI-08 ME: 135/162 (83.3%) vs 127/153 (83.0%), difference 0.3 (95% CI -8.6, 9.2); non-inferiority demonstrated

pivotal_trials.trial_name: DORI-05 and DORI-06 (two Phase 3 cUTI studies)
pivotal_trials.design: DORI-05: phase 3 multicenter randomized double-blind active-controlled non-inferiority study vs levofloxacin; DORI-06: phase 3 noncomparative open-label study (doripenem-treated subjects compared to levofloxacin-treated subjects in DORI-05)
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with complicated urinary tract infections, including pyelonephritis (1171 randomized)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoint: microbiological response at test-of-cure visit in the ME and mMITT populations
pivotal_trials.n: 1171 adults randomized across the two cUTI studies
pivotal_trials.result: DORI-05 ME microbiological eradication: doripenem 230/280 (82.1%) vs levofloxacin 221/265 (83.4%), difference -1.3% (95% CI -8.0%, 5.5%); DORI-06 (noncomparative, open-label) doripenem 209/250 (83.6%), with difference 0.2% (95% CI -6.6, 7.0) relative to the DORI-05 levofloxacin arm; non-inferiority supported

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥5%) were headache, nausea, diarrhea, rash and phlebitis. In cUTI, headache occurred in 16% (vs levofloxacin 15%); in cIAI, nausea 12% (vs meropenem 9%), diarrhea 11% (vs 11%), anemia 10% (vs 5%). Serious hypersensitivity (anaphylactic) reactions and C. difficile-associated diarrhea were warnings.
target_moa: Carbapenem (beta-lactam) antibacterial; bactericidal via inhibition of bacterial cell wall biosynthesis by inactivating multiple penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs)

advisory_committee.vote: NDA 22-106 was not referred to an advisory committee

summary.text: DORIBAX (doripenem for injection) is a synthetic carbapenem beta-lactam approved under a standard-review 505(b)(1) NDA for complicated intra-abdominal and complicated urinary tract infections, supported by four Phase 3 trials (three non-inferiority comparative studies and one noncomparative, open-label study, DORI-06); the application was not referred to an advisory committee and was approved on the first review cycle.
